course_name_en: Modeling and Animation Techniques for 3D Objects
prerequisites: Familiarity with the basic functions of BLENDER software, for example, through video tutorials.

learning_outcomes.text: Students master basic 3D modeling techniques such as box modeling based on polygonal meshes and freeform surfaces based on curves.
Students know and can apply basic computer animation techniques, especially keyframe animation, inverse kinematics methods, animation of physical systems, and simple character animation.
Students can effectively illuminate virtual scenes and apply suitable shaders and textures to surfaces.
Students can implement these skills exemplarily through their own programming and in a commercial computer animation system, and render for the respective output medium.
Students know the techniques for computer-aided modeling and animation of 3D objects.
Students are able to apply and deepen this knowledge and acquired skills in other areas of media informatics, e.g., in game programming or VR programming.
Students know professional software tools and techniques for 3D modeling and computer animation.
Students can assess their applicability for various fields of use.
Students can create complex 3D models and generate animations using a professional computer graphics and animation tool.
This also includes surface design with textures and shaders, as well as the effective use of lighting.
Students can research subject-specific topics for this module and consolidate them into a technical presentation.
Students develop complex 3D models and optimize them by integrating other media, e.g., audio or video recordings.
Students who have successfully completed this module can present the results of their homework and describe their solutions and methods in writing and orally.
They have worked on projects and their homework in teams.
Work results will be presented in a self-prepared technical lecture and subsequently discussed in plenum.
Students can assess their qualifications acquired in this module in the context of their future professional field and apply them professionally in the future.

syllabus_topics: Modeling with splines: Curves and surfaces
Techniques and design principles of animation
Fundamentals of textures, shaders, and rendering
Light - global and local illumination models - scene lighting
assessment_rules: Graded assessment can be either a presentation (approx. 30-40 minutes with a 5-15 page written elaboration) or a written project report (approx. 10-15 pages with a 30-minute explanation). An ungraded experimental work is also required, consisting of about 5 experiments.
